questions.text: In what way do expert systems differ fundamentally from machine learning models?
options: Expert systems rely on explicit, human-provided rules, whereas machine learning models learn patterns directly from data.
Expert systems learn from large datasets, while machine learning uses fixed rules.
Expert systems use fuzzy logic exclusively, while machine learning uses binary logic.
Expert systems are designed for unstructured problems, while machine learning is for structured problems.
questions.correctAnswer: Expert systems rely on explicit, human-provided rules, whereas machine learning models learn patterns directly from data.
questions.explanation:
An expert system applies rules supplied by human experts, while machine learning identifies patterns from training examples.

Student note: Both approaches need evaluation; learning from data does not make a model automatically reliable.
